title: ColorOp in shaders only operate in limited range which cause clipping in bright areas
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.3 Stable

### System information

Windows 10, Godot 4.3 Stable

### Issue description

If you apply Color Operations to images, the operations are performed in the 8-bit space only. Which means, if the brightness exceeds 1, it will not be extended (like it have to) but will be clipping to 1 and will be grayed out on the final image.

#### Here is the overlay with central area as gray:

(which will not change the luminosity)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19c51e6b-aa39-4b41-84d8-0e9cecfb5f96)

#### Here is the overlay with white center:

(the sky is now clamped into 1, it is in fact Darker, than it used to be, and auto exposure lit up the landscape):

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/055e97ce-b81a-42d1-95b9-ea942b4e7b18)

When someone applies effects that supposed to make the image brighter, the last thing they expect is to get a darker image with the loss of details. And since the majority of games have bright areas, these effects are barely usable.

#### The desired result

Instead, it would be nice to make it the same as in other apps, where it can operate in the same range as the original vector and can in fact be much brighter than 0-1 range. Otherwise, half of these operations are barely usable, since they can only be safely used to make the image darker.

### Steps to reproduce

Use ColorOp node with any mode that makes the original image brighter.
It will in areas of 0-1, but will cause clipping in 1+
